sourceInformation.tech: Three.js 0.180.0 WebGPU/TSL with WebGL2 fallback; Rapier 0.19.3; Web Audio; Gamepad API; esbuild 0.28.2
sourceInformation.artDirection: Procedural cel-shaded savanna, ink outlines, cross-hatching and paper grain
sourceInformation.animation: Three.js AnimationMixer, authored skeletal clips and procedural motion
sourceInformation.audio: Original synthesized music, effects and seeded gibberish voices; music defaults to 10%
sourceInformation.online: AI Hub Protocol v1 shared-world co-op for 1–4; BroadcastChannel same-computer co-op
sourceInformation.testing: Headless scripted simulation and complete campaign through all three endings; Playwright 1.63.0; virtual standard gamepad, touch profiles and offline audio; Chromium WebGPU/WebGL2, WebKit and Firefox; 24 viewport combinations; official Hub harness and two-player co-op. No physical controller or real iOS hardware.
sourceInformation.research: Provided PLAN.md and TASK.md; official AI Hub Session Protocol v1 README, client 1.4.0 and harness; local Three.js source and installed testing-toolkit help. Published font and Apache license notices.

testingFeedback: 24 gameplay or presentation issues found and corrected. Concurrent viewport capture and shared-machine memory failures were handled separately by serializing checks and reducing session graphics load.

7 game-breaking issues: movement after skipping the opening, unrelated cargo failing a contract, graphics starving session results, an uninitialized held-map texture on WebGPU, joining-player input actions missing the host simulation, an opaque windshield blocking the driving view, and an escaped convoy leaving a required contract active.
The input-driven complete campaign, including twists, both bark errands, a failed cargo retry and all three endings; it exposed interactions that isolated system checks missed.
The title-only smoke check was least informative about gameplay; it could not expose bugs that required a mission or a physical-map interaction.
engineFeedback: The same TSL cel and ink pipeline works on WebGPU and the WebGL2 fallback.
Yes. Canvas textures need an initialized rendering context before WebGPU upload, and expensive software frames can delay multiplayer messages.
The seeded simulation connecting fire, survival, weapons, vehicles, contracts, world consequences and co-op.
Keeping graphics construction and software rendering from blocking the session protocol.
None. The engine packages are unmodified; shaders, procedural assets and gameplay are application code.
A lighter explicit renderer-start phase and clearer cross-backend diagnostics for canvas textures and multiple render targets.
promptFeedback: The original setting, interacting systems and verified rendering recipes gave the game a clear identity.
The boundary between a vertical slice and the complete campaign was unusually broad.
Making the many survival, story and multiplayer systems work together through an entire campaign.
Use one machine-readable acceptance list shared by the plan, task and feature-coverage tests.

aiHub.name: Fare Cry
aiHub.description: Work both sides of a dying company-state in a first-person mercenary campaign. Read the wind, burn the grass, keep your gun working and decide what happens to the last honest ledger.
aiHub.controls: WASD / sticks move; mouse / right stick look; LMB / R2 fire; E / Square use; M / D-pad Up map; H heal; P bark; Esc pause.
